A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProEval and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E. All 50 pages were compared; the appendices are identical in text and rendered content.

before.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 report original performance-estimation and failure-discovery experiments, including human validation. Appendices C and E contain additional results and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments, human validation and appendix analyses, with limited corrections to reported diversity scores.

M1.justification: GP prior learning, GMM source selection, Bayesian quadrature acquisition and SS/SS-Gen/TSS procedures are unchanged. The shortened Section 2.2.3 heading does not indicate a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine benchmarks, text/image domains, Default/New Model/New Bench scenarios and generated StrategyQA/GSM8K tasks. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The random-sampling and LR/RF with IS/LURE baselines, failure-generation comparators including Rand-Anchor-Gen, and Appendix E source-selection comparisons remain unchanged. Consolidating duplicate rows in Table 1 preserves comparator participation.

E3.justification: Section 3.1.2 revises the documented overall-diversity metric by replacing H_norm/100 with H_norm. Other evaluation settings remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The CoT and embedding-model ablations, negative-transfer/source-selection studies, cross-modality experiment and 80-question human validation study are retained. No additional robustness test, ablation or case study is introduced.

E5.justification: The reported five-run performance-estimation and ten-run failure-discovery procedures retain the same standard-deviation and SEM reporting. Appendix E statistical procedures are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes Rand-Anchor-Gen's reported overall diversity from 0.99 to 0.74 on StrategyQA and from 1.00 to 0.75 on GSM8K. Proposed-method scores and appendix results remain unchanged; Table 1 merely consolidates identical NB/NM entries.

T1.justification: The composite-diversity definition in Section 3.1.2 removes an extra division by 100 from already normalized topic entropy, changing the mathematical definition as written. Assumptions 1–2, Theorem 3 and its Appendix B proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same framework contributions, theoretical guarantees, 8–65x sampling-efficiency claim and 2–5x failure-discovery claim.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the assertion that TSS-RPF achieves the highest diversity and surpasses all methods with a qualified interpretation that its diversity matches or nears Rand-Anchor-Gen. Other mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Feature/kernel configurations, source-selection details, dataset sizes and generator prompts remain unchanged, including Appendices C–E. The code and data access link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The literature review, bibliography and positioning relative to prior research are unchanged. The new ICML 2026 footnote records publication of a shorter version of the same work.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the Section 2.2.3 heading, rewrites the diversity interpretation, adds a publication footnote and updates the date. Paragraph breaks receive limited editing while the overall organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 merges identical NB/NM rows for BQ-RPF and BQ-RPF Rounded and adjusts column widths. Minor spacing and page-break changes accompany text reflow; figures and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves internal consistency by correcting the diversity normalization and two Table 3 entries, and replacing an unsupported superiority claim with a more defensible comparison. These are useful local accuracy improvements. The correction remains incomplete: Section 3.1.2 still discusses diversity scores of at least 0.90, although its stated normalized components and equal weights cap the score at 0.75.
